searchText: <@393119312350543872> is t8ntool a tool/protocol/mode that needs to be run through retesteth? Or is it a real CLI tool that can be used by itself? I mean: is this a a real command line, as seen in retesteth.ethdevops.io? `t8ntool -t BlockchainTests -- --all -j2 --filltests` Another subject: given that GeneralStateTests is included inside of BlockchainTests, why run GeneralStateTests separately? ... and what is BCGeneralStateTests in retesteth.ethdevops.io? There's no folder with that name in the tests repo nor UnitTests Something (disk? fs in memory?) runs out of space ... should I just make the image bigger or is there something wrong? `$ ./dretesteth.sh -t GeneralStateTests -- --testpath ~/tests --vmtraceraw --poststate --fullstate --all ... ERROR(11): failed writing output: write /dev/shm/ff5db0fe-3caa-4c11-a2f8-2b82d1e4dc87/outAlloc.json: no space left on device` Yes its a real tool that can be used for other dev purposes as well. Such as transaction execution and debug. No, retesteth cmd interface is different to t8ntool, it manages test generation and execution. T8ntool just takes files with data and output result If other clients implement t8ntool, retesteth can be used to generate tests using their evm Its 2 different formats. BC means blockchain. That is used by hive to run in blackbox for all the clients that does not support tests. State test format is simplier and used by custom test runner tools by all the teams. To run tests faster retesteth attempt to create intermediate communication files (inputs for t8ntool) on memory drive. Check that you have reserved some space for shm
